description: Whether a floor with nothing holding it runs away, and what holds it. On the shipped input the fit puts floors above the 80%-clear point on problems only competent players have attempted — an easy problem and a high floor explain those outcomes equally — and their ratings run off the bottom of the scale. `w001` / `w01` / `w1` add the RANDOM USER at that weight per row: a synthetic player who has answered every corpus problem at one over its legal moves, ability pinned infinitely low, so it acts on the floor alone; w1 is the player injected as an ordinary user's worth of rows. `lr_half` asks the other question — whether the runaway is a property of the optimization rather than of the objective — by halving BOTH learning rates and doubling the budget, which holds the delivered work fixed. THE BASELINE IS THE `all` ARM OF THE bot_temperatures PANEL, not an arm here: same seeds, same machine, same attempt frontier, whole problems held out, so within a seed the arms hold aside the same problems; the tabulation must check the two panels' pins agree before pairing. What is read is the floor distribution, the slope distribution and the rating's low tail beside the held-out likelihood — the likelihood alone cannot see the failure this panel is about.
